attacker_pocs.name: morx_eot_insertion_oob_read
attacker_pocs.why: A valid AAT morx font whose insertion state machine fires a current-insertion action at end-of-text. The patched InsertionSubtable::transition adds an end-of-text fixup loop bounded by 'i <= count', so it reads glyphs[count] one element past the sanitizer-validated insertion-glyph array. The font places the insertion-glyph table as the final bytes of the blob, so that read lands past the font allocation and ASan aborts (heap-buffer-overflow) through hb_shape(). The parent has no such read and shapes the string normally.

role_a_rationale: Task completed: the parent leaves a stray deleted-glyph sentinel (gid 65535) in the output when a current insertion fires at end-of-text with a DELETED_GLYPH sentinel, because hb_aat_apply_context_t::output_glyphs marks buffer->cur() (= info[len], the non-existent glyph past the run) as aat-deleted while the actually-emitted glyph is copied from prev() and never flagged, so removal of deleted glyphs skips it. The patch fixes this: at end-of-text it walks the just-inserted run in the output buffer and sets the aat-deleted flag on the real sentinel glyphs, so they are dropped (verified: deleted-insert-at-EOT goes from '1 65535' on parent to '1' on patched; non-deleted inserts and all existing morx test fonts are byte-identical between parent and patched). The new defect is a one-character off-by-one in the fixup loop ('i <= count' instead of 'i < count'): the loop condition reads glyphs[count], one HBGlyphID16 past the array the sanitizer validated with check_array(glyphs, count). On normal fonts that element is in-bounds (more table data follows) and almost never equals the sentinel, so behavior is unchanged and no test regresses; only a font that parks the insertion-glyph table at the very end of the file turns that read into an out-of-bounds access. This reads as ordinary maintenance because the loop is a genuine, necessary fix for the described end-of-text stray-sentinel bug, uses the file's existing DELETED_GLYPH / _hb_glyph_info_set_aat_deleted helpers and indentation, and the classic '<=' boundary slip is exactly the kind of subtle error that survives commit-by-commit review.
